Standing-teams programme · operating policies

Which recommendations should set the programme's limits?

I recommend applying all eight: together they set spending limits, reduce repeated permission asks, and clarify what the teams may do. The sender's reviewer advises deciding separately on lasting access grants and permanent run deletion.

Choose the main answer below, then select any recommendations in the form. Unchecked policies keep their current defaults. You can select the six reversible policies now and leave the two harder-to-reverse policies unchanged.

The eight choices

1. Usage ceiling

Recommendation: at most 15 weekly quota points per 24 hours; stop and report at 50% of the week. Cheaper-model mode stays on. Default: cheaper-model mode on, no ceiling.

Reversible

2. Remove unused code

Recommendation: delete about 8,000 lines across the unused control stack, duplicate plan editor and three dormant plan families. This code remains in history. Default: keep it; the board shrinks by 10% rather than 25%.

Reversible from history

3. Team access from a notification

Recommendation: allow grants with no expiry until revoked, and list active grants in every daily digest. Default: grants only by link or command line, up to 30 days.

Hard to take back · decide separately

4. Reviews in Notification Hub

Recommendation: answer reviews and goal close-outs in the Hub, as run reviews already are. Default: keep them in the command line and web console.

Reversible

5. Permanent deletion of old runs

Recommendation: let agents permanently delete any old run belonging to the same owner without asking. Default: agents must ask.

Irreversible · deleted runs are gone

6. Fewer repeat permission requests

Recommendation: agents you launched may notify and ask without a separate grant each time. Default: a grant each time. Eight of the last eleven permission requests were for this.

Reversible

7. Fewer “turn finished” alerts

Recommendation: mute them and send one daily digest at normal urgency. They made up 2,448 of 3,366 notifications in 30 days. Default: leave notifications unchanged.

Reversible

8. Supervision objective

Recommendation: cover research and standing-team owners, and enable the objective last. Default: leave unchanged and enable it last.

Reversible

Keep all eight defaults

Tap “Choose this,” select policies in the form if you chose the first answer, then send.

What happens when you approve

The selected policies are recorded and handed to the teams that apply them. An unselected policy stays at its current safe default.

If you do not answer

All eight defaults stay in force, and the programme continues without waiting for you.

Second opinion. The sender's reviewer agrees the six reversible changes can be considered together, and recommends a separate answer on notification-based lasting grants and permanent deletion.
